newsitem.title: USA: U.S domestic auto sales off 6.7 pct Dec 21-31 - CNW.
newsitem.headline: U.S domestic auto sales off 6.7 pct Dec 21-31 - CNW.

text.p: U.S. domestic auto sales fell 6.7 percent in the 10-day period December 21-31 compared with the same period a year ago, according to a CNW Marketing/Research report released Thursday.
Domestic car sales dropped to 197,804 from 217,655, CNW said. Domestic truck sales fell 4.2 percent to 208,236, according to the report.
Import car sales dipped 5.7 percent to 79,587, and import truck sales fell 6.0 percent to 16,304, the report said.
CNW said 36.8 percent of the vehicles were leased, up from 34.2 percent in the same period last year.
About 15.2 million vehicles were sold in the United States from January through the final week in December 1996, CNW said.
"In large part, automaker sales will indicate stronger showing because dealers reported many November sales in early December," CNW said.
"Regardless, the year ended relatively flat giving a barely dimmer view for 1997," it said.
